name: J. Kellogg, soap and candle manufactory

proprietors.name: Joseph Kellogg
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Joseph Kellogg is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at soap_and_candle_maker in the west division (slot trade_households:persons/male/40_49/west/family/trade:soap_and_candle_maker:003), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. Here the head is not merely the proprietor of the house — the head IS what bought it, because no count of this class was ever printed to be short of.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a soap and candle manufactory kept by a west-division household deals this house onto West Water Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because the resident band drew a soap and candle maker the town was short of, and the trade names the house he keeps. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. The head who keeps it is ordered onto the scene date and to nothing narrower, and a keeping is not an opening; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read yankee: Joseph Kellogg (yankee). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real soap and candle manufactory in the west division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn with the head.

trade_head.note: A TRADE HEAD, NOT A SHORTFALL AND NOT A ROOF. The December 1835 State census's eighteen lines never reach this class, so the order book holds no bucket to point at and no count of it can be short; and nothing in data/structures/ is a soap and candle manufactory, so there is no committed building to buy the firm either. What IS committed is the man: the resident band drew Joseph Kellogg at soap and candle maker because the 1839 trade table says the town was short of the trade, and a soap and candle maker works a manufactory, and the register prints one — Daniel Elston & [Co.], the Chicago Soap and Candle Manufactory — against a census with no line for the trade. The house is withdrawn with the head.

basis.note: the resident band drew 1 head(s) at soap and candle maker in the west division and a soap and candle maker works a manufactory, and the register prints one — Daniel Elston & [Co.], the Chicago Soap and Candle Manufactory — against a census with no line for the trade. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: form 1 of the naming guide, the corpus's commonest signature, which is the sole maker's form of 'Daniel Elston & [Co.]' once the firm is cut to the one keeper it is. The goods line is the trade line the register prints under Daniel Elston & [Co.] and the Chicago Soap and Candle Manufactory.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: the retirement of the head himself, a re-cut of the order book that no longer orders his person bucket, or a source naming a real house of this class; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
